::: {#rem-receptive-field-growth}

#### How fast a receptive field grows

A $k \times k$ [convolutional layer](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-convolutional-layer) with [stride](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-stride) 1 makes each side of the [receptive field](#def-receptive-field) $k - 1$ pixels longer.
So $L$ such layers of $3 \times 3$ [filters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-filter) give a receptive field of $(2L + 1) \times (2L + 1)$ pixels,
away from the edges of the image.
@sol-receptive-field found $L = 2$ layers and a $5 \times 5$ block.
[Pooling](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-pooling) and [stride](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-stride) make it grow faster,
since each step of a later layer then moves farther across the input [@dumoulin2016guide].

:::
